text:
### Observed differences

- Participation is essentially unchanged: A15, A17, A18, A24 and A35 appear in all 200 traces in both windows, while each of A14, A16 and A19 appears in roughly 30–38 in 100 traces (about 60–71 of 200 earlier, 58–77 later), with the three rates summing to about one appearance per trace in both windows. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]
- The order between the two activity groups flipped completely. Earlier, whenever an activity from {A14, A16, A19} co-occurred with one of {A15, A17, A18}, it always came first (e.g., A14 preceded A15 in about 30 in 100 traces, covering all co-occurring cases); in the later window the trio always came first (e.g., A15 preceded A16 in about 29 in 100 traces, again all co-occurring cases). [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL006, REL007, REL010, REL011, REL014, REL017]
- The order around the anchors A20 and A24 also flipped in every trace. Earlier, A20 and A24 each came after the {A14, A16, A19} activity and before A15/A17/A18 (e.g., A20 preceded A15 in 200 of 200 traces); in the later window A20 and A24 each came after A15/A17/A18 and before the {A14, A16, A19} activity (A15 preceded A20 in 200 of 200). [REL004, REL005, REL008, REL009, REL012, REL013, REL015, REL016, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021]
- Outgoing transitions were rewired accordingly. Earlier, A14, A16 and A19 led exclusively to A20 (100% of observed outgoing transitions); in the later window they led exclusively to A25. A15, A17 and A18 led to A25 in about 30–38 of 100 outgoing transitions earlier and never later, and to A20 in about 28–36 of 100 later and never earlier. A24's successors changed from A15/A18/A17 (about 37/33/30 in 100) to A19/A16/A14 (about 39/29/33 in 100), and A35's from A16/A14/A19 (about 35/30/35 in 100) to A17/A15/A18 (about 36/33/31 in 100). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]
- Event-position distances corroborate this: A25 followed A24 by 4 positions earlier and by 2 positions later, while A20 followed A35 by 2 positions earlier and 4 positions later — consistent with a one-activity segment and a three-activity segment trading places between these anchors. [LAG001, LAG002]
- Within the trio {A15, A17, A18}, activities still appear in both mutual orders in similar shares in both windows (e.g., A15 led to A17 in about 40 of 100 outgoing transitions earlier, A17 led to A15 in about 31 of 100 later), so the internal flexibility of that group did not change. [DIR002, DIR004, DIR005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that two segments of the process exchanged their positions. In the earlier window, each trace ran A35 into one of A14/A16/A19, then A20 and A24, then the trio A15, A17 and A18 in varying order, which exited to A25. In the later window, A35 ran into the trio A15/A17/A18, which preceded A20 and A24, and the single activity from {A14, A16, A19} ran after them and exited to A25 — that is, the one-activity segment {A14, A16, A19} and the three-activity segment {A15, A17, A18} swapped places around the fixed anchors A35, A24, A20 and A25, and the handover to A25 moved from the trio to the single activity. [DIR001, DIR003, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, REL004, REL008, REL009, LAG001, LAG002]

The support is direct and consistent: all 21 relation items crossing the two segments or connecting them to A20/A24 flip from one fixed order to the exact opposite with co-occurrence rates essentially unchanged; the direction profiles show the matching rewiring of exits (A20 vs A25) and feeds (A24 and A35 each now lead into the other segment); and the step-distance changes match the segment sizes. The volume of qualifying evidence also far exceeds what an unchanged process produces: 31 control-flow items against roughly 0.41 expected by chance, each difference larger than in about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR004, DIR005, REL001, REL008, REL015, REL020, LAG001, LAG002]

Limitations: the 31 items overlap heavily (many pairs share the same traces), so they describe one coherent difference rather than independent findings; the evidence cannot distinguish a single swap of the two segments from two coordinated relocations that produce the same orderings; and a variant retaining the old order could persist below the resolution of 200 traces per window, since no trace in either window shows the opposite order. [REL004, REL008, LAG001]
